concepts.why: Treats the text as compiling and running although public class Greeting is saved as Hello.java and the println line lacks its semicolon, i.e. assumes the file name is independent of the class name and that the computer fills in what the programmer meant (also reads args[1] as Ann, which is args[0]).

concepts.quote: It prints Hi, Ann and then Bye.
concepts.why: Assumes the program runs and prints straight from the saved text, ignoring that javac must first succeed (it will not) and that, even if compiled, args[1] with one argument throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException so nothing is printed.
Claims the commented-out line // System.out.println("Bye"); executes, i.e. treats a comment as a statement that is run; that line never runs.
